newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley's Wien more positive on U.S. stocks.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley's Wien more positive on U.S. stocks.

text.p: Morgan's Stanley's chief U.S. equity strategist Byron Wien has changed his model portfolio, putting more money into stocks after reversing his previously bearish position.

According to Morgan's U.S. strategist Leah Modigliani, Wien raised his stocks allocation by five percent to 85 percent. Cash was cut to fifteen percent. The model portfolio is made up of stocks and cash, with cash fluctuating between zero and 30 percent.
"He said he will probably put another five percent in stocks in the future," she said.
On Friday, Wien changed his view on the market, reversing his bearish stance, Modigliani said.

"Now he thinks rates are more likely to go lower because of some signs of temporary weakness in the economy. Therefore, he thinks there may be a ten percent upside to the market in the next six months. And with that outlook, there's a better place to be than in cash," Modigliani said.
Wien favors interest-rate sensitive stocks, such as the financial services sector and money center banks.
